I'll review EVAL-01 by calling the actions to build and submit the threat model.

Let me first call get-review-context to retrieve the full context including the submission token:

```
get-review-context(issueKey="EVAL-01")
```

Now I'll analyze the security design for threats using STRIDE:

**Key Issues Identified:**
1. Refresh token stored in **plaintext** app storage (not iOS Keychain)
2. Biometrics only protect screen unlock, not the token or banking operations
3. Token exposed in device backups
4. No cryptographic binding to Secure Enclave
5. No token lifecycle management

Building threat model with 8 critical/high threats:

```json
{
  "schema": "redline.threatmodel.v1",
  "issueKey": "EVAL-01",
  "sketch": {
    "components": ["iOS Banking App", "Face ID Sensor", "App Storage", "Banking Backend API", "Device Backup", "iOS Keychain"],
    "dataStores": ["App Storage", "Device Backup"],
    "externalServices": ["Banking Backend API"],
    "trustBoundaries": ["Device Boundary", "App Sandbox", "Network"],
    "dataClasses": ["credentials"],
    "exposure": "internal",
    "llmFeatures": false
  },
  "threats": [
    {
      "stride": "InformationDisclosure",
      "title": "Refresh token stored in plaintext in app storage",
      "scenario": "Attacker with physical device access, iTunes/iCloud backup access, or forensic tools extracts the plaintext refresh token from app storage, granting persistent authentication to the victim's bank account without needing password or biometric.",
      "component": "App Storage",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 5,
      "evidence": [{"quote": "stores the refresh token in plain app storage"}],
      "asvs": ["V8.3.4", "V8.3.7"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-312", "CWE-522"],
      "plainLanguage": "Anyone with your phone or backup can read your login token and access your bank account",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Cryptographically protected token storage",
        "given": "the mobile banking app needs to maintain user sessions across app restarts",
        "when": "the app stores the refresh token",
        "then": "it must use iOS Keychain with kSecAttrAccessibleWhenPasscodeSetThisDeviceOnly and biometric-gated access, never plaintext app storage"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Spoofing",
      "title": "Stolen refresh token allows full account impersonation",
      "scenario": "Attacker who obtained the refresh token (via backup, physical access, or memory dump) uses it to authenticate to the banking backend as the victim, performing transactions, transferring money, and accessing sensitive account details without victim's password or biometric.",
      "component": "Banking Backend API",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 5,
      "evidence": [{"quote": "stores the refresh token in plain app storage"}],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-522"],
      "plainLanguage": "A stolen login token lets someone pretend to be you and transfer your money",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Device binding for refresh tokens",
        "given": "an attacker obtains a valid refresh token",
        "when": "they attempt to use it to authenticate from a different device or context",
        "then": "the backend must validate device fingerprint, detect anomalies, and require re-authentication"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "ElevationOfPrivilege",
      "title": "Biometrics only protect screen unlock, not banking operations",
      "scenario": "Attacker who bypasses the screen lock (via iOS vulnerability, guessed passcode, shoulder-surfed unlock code, or accessing already-unlocked device) immediately gains full banking access because biometric verification doesn't gate the refresh token, transactions, or sensitive operations.",
      "component": "iOS Banking App",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 5,
      "evidence": [{"quote": "uses biometrics only to unlock the screen"}],
      "asvs": ["V2.8.3"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-287"],
      "plainLanguage": "Your fingerprint only locks the screen, not your bank - bypassing the lock gives full access",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Biometric verification for sensitive operations",
        "given": "a user has configured biometric authentication",
        "when": "they attempt to view account details, initiate a transaction, or access sensitive features",
        "then": "the app must require fresh biometric verification for each operation, not just screen unlock"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "InformationDisclosure",
      "title": "Refresh token exposed in unencrypted device backups",
      "scenario": "User's iCloud or iTunes backup contains the plaintext refresh token; attacker with backup access (compromised iCloud account, stolen laptop with backup, shared family computer, forensic extraction) extracts and reuses the token to access the banking account.",
      "component": "Device Backup",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 5,
      "evidence": [{"quote": "stores the refresh token in plain app storage"}],
      "asvs": ["V8.3.7"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-311"],
      "plainLanguage": "Your login token sits in your phone backup where anyone with backup access can steal it",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Exclude tokens from backups",
        "given": "the app stores authentication credentials",
        "when": "the device is backed up to iCloud or iTunes",
        "then": "sensitive tokens must be stored in Keychain with appropriate attributes to exclude them from backups"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Tampering",
      "title": "Jailbroken device allows token manipulation",
      "scenario": "On a jailbroken device, malware or attacker with root access reads, modifies, or replaces the refresh token in app storage, allowing them to inject their own authentication token, corrupt the user's session, or maintain persistent backdoor access to the banking app.",
      "component": "App Storage",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [{"quote": "stores the refresh token in plain app storage"}],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-921"],
      "plainLanguage": "On a jailbroken phone, malware can read or change your login token",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Jailbreak detection and mitigation",
        "given": "the app runs on potentially compromised devices",
        "when": "the app launches or accesses sensitive data",
        "then": "it must detect jailbreak indicators and either refuse to run or require additional authentication"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "ElevationOfPrivilege",
      "title": "No cryptographic binding between biometric and token",
      "scenario": "Attacker who compromises the app process (via memory dump, debugging tools on jailbroken device, or runtime manipulation) extracts the refresh token from memory because it's not cryptographically protected by the Secure Enclave or gated by biometric verification for each retrieval.",
      "component": "iOS Banking App",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 5,
      "evidence": [{"quote": "uses biometrics only to unlock the screen"}],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-311"],
      "plainLanguage": "The login token isn't locked by your fingerprint, so malware can steal it from the app's memory",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Cryptographic binding to biometric authentication",
        "given": "the app needs to protect the refresh token in memory",
        "when": "the app retrieves the token for use",
        "then": "it must be encrypted with a key accessible only via biometric authentication through the Secure Enclave"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Repudiation",
      "title": "No token rotation or lifecycle management",
      "scenario": "Once a refresh token is compromised (via backup, theft, or memory dump), it continues working indefinitely until the user changes their password, giving the attacker an extended window (weeks or months) for unauthorized access that may go undetected until the victim notices suspicious transactions.",
      "component": "Banking Backend API",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [{"quote": "stores the refresh token"}],
      "asvs": ["V3.5.2"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-613"],
      "plainLanguage": "Once your login token is stolen, it works forever until you change your password",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Token rotation and lifecycle controls",
        "given": "a refresh token may be compromised without user knowledge",
        "when": "the token is used or significant time passes",
        "then": "the backend must rotate tokens regularly, invalidate on security events, and log all token usage"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "ElevationOfPrivilege",
      "title": "Shared device allows unauthorized family member access",
      "scenario": "User adds a family member's fingerprint to their device for convenience; that person can now unlock the device and access the banking app with full account privileges because the biometric system doesn't distinguish between enrolled users, and the refresh token isn't bound to a specific biometric identity.",
      "component": "Face ID Sensor",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [{"quote": "uses biometrics only to unlock the screen"}],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-287"],
      "plainLanguage": "Anyone whose fingerprint unlocks your phone can access your bank account",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Biometric identity verification",
        "given": "multiple users may have biometric access to the same device",
        "when": "a user authenticates with their biometric",
        "then": "the app must verify the specific biometric identity matches the account owner or require additional verification"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

Now calling submit-threat-model with the JSON:

```
submit-threat-model(
  issueKey="EVAL-01",
  submissionToken=<token_from_get_review_context>,
  threatModelJson=<json_string_above>
)
```
